claims.statement: The revised EU buildings framework is intended to accelerate solar on residential and non-residential buildings, while actual suitability still depends on technical, economic, and structural conditions.

contrary_evidence: The EU source explicitly says national criteria and site suitability matter, so a roof option alone does not create a viable project.
Existing residential buildings are not generally required by the cited directive to install solar.

economics.acquisition_route: Family renewable-energy network, commercial property managers, energy auditors, and algorithmic roof screening
economics.founder_net_worth_path: A possible but unvalidated path is 40 transfers a year at roughly 40000 PLN contribution plus recurring portfolio rights, supporting a valuable founder-owned development platform
economics.founder_time: Initially 12-20 hours per week, with survey, legal, and owner follow-up delegated
economics.gross_margin_basis: Expected 65-80% before founder pay if surveys and legal drafting are bought only after staged qualification
economics.payback: Unvalidated; two to four successful site transfers could repay setup and failed-diligence costs
economics.pricing: Unvalidated: 20000-80000 PLN per accepted or closed site, potentially with a 1-2% project success fee
economics.retention_or_repeat: Developers can buy repeated site batches; owner options are finite and require replenishment

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A growing exclusive site portfolio, standardized diligence evidence, and landlord-to-landlord referrals make the pipeline harder to reproduce
fingerprint.customer: Polish commercial solar developers and energy-as-a-service investors seeking de-risked project pipeline
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Begin through the founder's family installer relationships, regional property managers, energy auditors, and data-scored direct outreach to building owners
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Option underused roofs for 18-36 months, screen them with data and partner surveys, then charge 20000-80000 PLN per transferred bankable site plus an optional closing success fee
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The developer or investor pays an assignment or development fee when it accepts a diligence package, signs the site rights, or reaches financial close
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A developer needs suitable non-residential sites but owner origination and early diligence are slow and fragmented

founder_fit: Uses Polish renewable-energy access and the parents' installer network
Data-led site screening suits the founder's analytical skills
Can start with options and outsourced surveys instead of owning generation assets
Does not require a public personal brand
risks: Poorly drafted options may be unenforceable or deter owners
Grid or structural failures can strand diligence spend
Conflicts with the family company must be disclosed and contractually managed

structure.commercial_archetype: Project-rights portfolio developer paid on option assignment or project close
structure.control_point: Exclusive, site-specific rooftop solar and storage development options
structure.critical_dependency: Enough optioned roofs must pass structural, grid, owner-consent, and buyer underwriting checks

thesis: Secure time-limited exclusive development options from Polish warehouse and SME property owners, perform low-cost solar and storage diligence, and transfer bankable site packages to EPCs or energy-as-a-service investors for a fee at signing or financial close.
title: Commercial-Roof Development Option Bank
uncertainties: Unknown developer willingness to pay for third-party originated options
Unknown option conversion rate and average time to close
Polish grid and property-law diligence requirements need specialist review
No owner or developer demand has been validated
